newsitem.title: PERU: Explosion heard near siege site in Peru - radio.
newsitem.headline: Explosion heard near siege site in Peru - radio.

text.p: Peruvian national radio reported a loud explosion had been heard early on Thursday near the site of the Japanese embassy residence, where Marxist rebels are holding 104 VIP hostages.
A Reuters photographer one block from the residence also said she heard an explosion. It could not be confirmed if the explosion came from within the residence.
"The explosion came from within the residence at the back part. We are trying to investigate it but we cannot get very close," Nestor Ramos, a police officer at the site told national radio.

Eye witnesses said before the explosion, heard around 1:45 A.M. local time (0645 GMT), they saw no unusual movement of police at the site, which has been under siege since last Tuesday when about 20 heavily-armed Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels stormed the residence.
The MRTA rebels were holding hostages, including government officials, Japanese VIPs and some foreign diplomats.

In the ninth day of the siege, the rebels and the Peruvian government were deadlocked over the guerrilla demand that their jailed comrades be released -- a demand President Alberto Fujimori has refused to consider.
